verses.1: To the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
verses.2: Happy is the one who shows concern for the poor and the needy; in a day of trouble, the LORD will deliver them.
verses.3: The LORD will protect them and preserve them in the land; He will not give them over to the hand of their enemy.
verses.4: The LORD will support them on the bed of affliction; You have turned all their couch away as they lie ill.
verses.5: I said, "O LORD, be gracious to me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against You."
verses.6: My enemies speak evil about me: "When will he die and his name be forgotten?"
verses.7: When someone comes to see me, he speaks idly, his heart gathers up wrongdoing for himself. He goes out and spreads it abroad.
verses.8: All my enemies conspire together against me. They plot evil against me.
verses.9: They have laid a treacherous charge against me: "The one who lies down will not rise again."
verses.10: Even the man who was my friend, in whom I trusted, the one who ate my bread, has turned his heel against me.
verses.11: But You, O LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up, and I will repay them.
verses.12: By this I know that You delight in me: that my enemy does not triumph over me.
verses.13: And in my innocence You uphold me, and You place me before You forever.
verses.14: Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, from eternity to eternity. Amen and Amen.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 10: "the one who ate my bread" reflects the Hebrew idiom for a close companion, not a literal meal.  
- v. 14: "Amen and Amen" is included as in the Hebrew, which uses the doubled form for emphasis.
